linkedin.title: Personalized news is currently broken, but it does not have to stay that way.
linkedin.body:
Most news apps today operate on a simple loop. They show you more of what you already clicked on, creating a feedback loop that narrows your world rather than expanding it. That is not personalization. That is just an echo chamber designed to keep you scrolling.

At Headlinne, we are building something different. Our roadmap is focused on moving away from engagement metrics and toward genuine relevance. We believe AI should act as a filter that helps you understand the world better, not just a tool to keep you addicted to headlines.

The next phase for us is about nuance. We are working on ways to help you see multiple perspectives on the same story without the noise. The goal is to provide clarity, not just volume. You should be able to get the facts you need in five minutes, so you can spend the rest of your day actually living your life.

story_card.headline: China accused of bypassing US tariffs via third countries
story_card.standfirst: A new US report reveals how Chinese goods are dodging levies through global trade routes.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: A new US report claims China is routing goods through countries with lower tariffs to avoid levies.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The US imposed high tariffs on Chinese imports. Companies sought ways to lower their tax bills.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This strategy undermines the US trade policy meant to protect domestic industries.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for potential US government crackdowns or new trade rules targeting these transit countries.

story_card.caption:
A new US government report details how China is allegedly avoiding trade tariffs through third party nations.

The report highlights a complex network where goods are funneled through countries with friendlier trade terms. This practice allows Chinese exporters to bypass higher costs originally set by the US. It raises questions about the effectiveness of current trade enforcement.
